To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a low‐viscosity histidine‐trypto‐phane‐ketoglutaratic acid solution (HTK), used as a flush solution for the initial graft rinsing, is superior to the standard flush solution University of Wisconsin (UW).
the combination of HTK flush and UW cold storage is superior compared to the individual use of HTK or UW solution.
a combination of HTK solution as initial flush and UW solution for subsequent preservation is more effective than a single use of either HTK or UW solution.

the development of novel strategies for liver preservation and transplantation.
the development and evaluation of novel methods of organ preservation.
the development of a new preservation solution for the organ transplantation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the combination of HTK and UW solution is superior to the single use either of HTK or UW solution in liver preservation.
the combination of HTK and UW solution for liver preservation provides a cumulative protective effect.

HTK solution, with its lower viscosity, is superior to UW solution as an initial flush, but the latter is still superior as a subsequent storage solution, and that combining these two solutions results in the best outcome in liver graft preservation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the combination of low‐viscosity histidine‐trytophan‐ketoglutaric acid solution for the initial graft flush and subsequent cold storage in UW solution represents a feasible improvement in organ preservation, which also reduces the amount of UW solution required for cold storage.
the use of HTK flush and UW storage is superior compared to the use of UW flush and UW storage or the single use of HTK.
the combination of HTK solution and UW solution provides an improved preservation of the liver.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the use of a low‐viscosity histidine‐trypto‐phan‐ketoglutaric acid (HTK) solution for initial graft flushing and subsequent storage in a University of Wisconsin (UW) solution is superior to the single use either solution in an extracellular perfusion model and in a rat liver transplantation model.

a low‐viscosity histidine‐trytophan‐ketoglutaric acid (HTK) solution is a suitable alternative to the standard University of Wisconsin (UW) solution for graft perfusion and flushing in liver preservation and transplantation.

we have shown that the use of a low‐viscosity perfusate for initial flushing of the liver graft, followed by cold storage in UW solution, is superior to the use of UW solution for both initial flushing and subsequent storage.
